newsitem.title: USA: Moderate drinking may be good for heart - study.
newsitem.headline: Moderate drinking may be good for heart - study.

text.p: While heavy drinking increases the likelihood of death from cardiovascular disease, moderate consumption may lessen the risk among men, researchers found.

According to a study published in the January 13 issue of the American Medical Association's Archives of Internal Medicine, there is a "significant decrease" in cardiovascular deaths among men who have two to six drinks per week.

The study, conducted by Dr. Carlos A. Camargo, Jr., and colleagues from Brigham and Women's Hospital and Harvard Medical School followed a group of 22,071 men for more than 10 years. The men ranged in age from 40 to 84 and had no history of heart attacks, strokes or cancer.

During the study, 1,206 men died, mostly of cancer and cardiovascular disorders. But men who drank two to four alcoholic beverages per week were 28 percent less likely to die from cardiovascular disorders, cancer and other causes then men who drank less than once a week.
The death rate was 51 percent higher among men who had two or more drinks per day.
"The difference between consumption of small and large amounts of alcohol may mean the difference between preventing and causing excess mortality," the researchers concluded.
Heavy drinkers were far more likely to die from lung cancer than men who had less than one drink a week.

Occasional drinkers were less likely to die from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, immunodeficiency disorders, Alzheimer's deisease and other degenative diseases of the central nervous system, the study found.
"We suggest that individuals discuss their drinking habits with their health care provider, who can help assess the health risks and benefits," the researchers said.
No conclusions could be drawn for women because the risk of breast cancer skews the data, the researchers said.
